correctness.rationale: For all k>=3 and m_i>=1, the canonical H-polar is a bounded graph Lipschitz polytope. Its extreme potentials have connected tight graphs and are integral; graph diameter two restricts to binary or three-level potentials. A centered binary potential has exact squared norm j(N-j)/N; three-level potentials have a+b-(a-b)^2/N. The maxima B and T are both achieved by feasible points (T used only for L>=2, and for L=1 T<=B). The global inball is centered at the origin by central symmetry. Farthest vertices determine the tangencies and antipodal orthogonality of all centers. Rank computations yield the parity/multiplicity dimension formulas, including ties and the all-singleton case. Final standard-library exact checker replayed finite profiles; those are not infinite proofs.

value.rationale: A whole infinite graph-polytope family acquires an exact canonical metric inradius depending only on N and the largest multipartite class, with a genuinely competing binary/ternary contact-facet mechanism. The entire incenter locus has an exact parity-sensitive affine dimension and examples have unbounded nonuniqueness, while close symmetric profiles exhibit unique centers. The result supplies geometric information that the known facet count and Ehrhart invariants do not evaluate; it is natural and potentially reusable in metric polytope comparisons.
